Where We Are

Recap: Four Stages of Preprocessing

Transformation

Recap: Data TypesNumbers get rescaled; discretization turns numbers into categories

The type of a column decides the tool

Three Branches of Transformation

Scaling Numbers

Why Scale at AllDistance-based models add up raw units, so the widest column decides

In raw Euclidean distance, the rpm difference dominates the cycle-time difference

The Evaluation Must Match DeploymentDefine what will be new at prediction time before splitting the records

Deployment questionUseful splitWhat a random row split can hide
Predict future eventsEarlier train; later testFuture information reaches training
Predict new machinesHold out whole machinesSame-machine patterns occur on both sides
Predict new customersHold out whole customersRepeated identity makes the test easier
A held-out row can still share an entity or future information with training

MachineRole

Testing new machines requires machines that training has never seen

Fitted Transformation StateFit learns parameters; transform reuses the saved parameters

StepFit on trainTransform new rows
Scalingmin, max or mean, SDreuse the same numbers
Encodingcategory vocabularyreuse the same columns
PCAcenter and axesproject onto the same axes
Fit once on training rows, then apply the saved state

Linear ScalersThree scalers, one shape: subtract a center, divide by a spread

Picking a scaler is picking how many bad rows it takes to move the answer

Min-Max Scalingx′ = (x − min) / (max − min) maps the training range onto [0, 1]

The minimum maps to 0, the maximum to 1. Fit both on train only

Demo: Fit on Train, Apply to TestTrain cycle times stay at 28, 32 and 36 seconds

1. Can a transformed test value exceed 1?   2. Does refitting change the training rows?
40 s

Answer: Reusing a ScalerAt test = 40, the saved training range produces 1.5

Fitting rowsmin / maxtrain 36 →test 40 →
Train only28 / 361.0001.500
Train + test28 / 400.6671.000
New observations can lie outside the fitted training range

Caveat: Min-Max and OutliersOne outlier is enough to squash every other value

The maximum defines the range, so the maximum defines everything

Z-Score StandardizationEach training column gets mean 0 and standard deviation 1

z = (x − μ) / σthe shape is untouched; only the axis is relabeled
A right tail stays a right tail. Standardizing does not make a column normal

Robust ScalingThe median and the IQR barely move when one row goes wrong

x′ = (x − median) / IQRIQR = interquartile range
The median moves to zero and the outliers stay far out. That is intended

Demo: Feature Scalers300 cycles from one computer numerical control (CNC) machine, both columns on one axis

1. Compare scalers with a mistyped rpm.   2. Did scaling repair the error or change the reference statistics?

Answer: Scaling and OutliersScaling changes the reference statistics, not the recorded event

ScalerReference statisticsEffect of an extreme value
MinMaxmin and maxclean values compress into a narrow range
Standardmean and SDcenter and spread can move
Robustmedian and IQRresists some extremes; keeps the outlier
Scaling changes representation; it does not validate or remove a value

Log TransformLog turns ratios into equal steps

log2(2x) − log2(x) = 1x > 0
Each doubling becomes the same gap. Normality is not guaranteed

Unit Vector NormalizationScale each row, not each column, to length 1

x′ = x / ‖x‖2then x′Ty′ is exactly the cosine similarity
Every row lands on the unit circle; the dot product is now cosine similarity

Encoding and Binning

Encoding vs BinningOne turns categories into numbers, the other turns numbers into categories

What the model can use decides which way you cross

Nominal and Ordinal CategoriesA numeric code can introduce order and spacing into the model

Nominal: no known order

ColorArbitrary code
red1
green2
blue3

Ordinal: a known order

SizeOrdered code
small1
medium2
large3
Color codes invent an order; size codes express an existing order

One-Hot EncodingOne indicator column per category, so no order is invented

x → ( 𝕀[x = c1], …, 𝕀[x = ck] )k categories become k columns whose sum is always 1
With an intercept, k one-hot columns are linearly dependent. Dropping one removes this dependency

Choosing an EncodingOrder, the number of categories and the model decide the encoding

Data meaningStarting choiceCheck
Unordered categoriesOne-hotWidth and unknown values
Known ordered levelsOrdinal codesThe supplied order matches the meaning
Text or many related categoriesLearned embeddingVocabulary, model version and validation
Start with the category meaning, then check width and held-out behavior

Demo: Categorical EncodersSix training rows; reuse their category vocabulary for test

1. Compare one-hot with integer codes.   2. Apply the fitted vocabulary to an unseen test color.
BEFORE
AFTER ·

Answer: An Unseen CategoryA fitted encoder needs an explicit policy for a new value

Encoder policyBlue at test timeConsequence
One-hot, ignore unknown[0, 0, 0, 0]keeps four fitted columns
Integer codes, unknown = -1-1unknown remains distinct
Add a test-only Blue columnfive columnschanges the fitted representation
Keep the fitted vocabulary; define how unknown values are represented

Vector EmbeddingA learned model maps each category to a short real vector

Distances now differ between pairs. In one-hot, every pair of categories is equally far apart

An Encoding Cannot Restore a Binned ValueBinning loses within-bin differences; encoding represents the resulting category

A numeric output does not imply that the original measurement was preserved

Why DiscretizeContinuous values give almost every row its own case

Four bins replace 29 values. Where the cuts go is the whole question

Binning by HistogramEqual width keeps the scale, equal frequency keeps the counts

width = (max − min) / kvscount = n / kthe same k, two different things held constant
Equal width: 26, 8, 1, 2, 3 rows. Equal frequency: 8 in every bin

Making Features

Hand-Crafted FeaturesNo column holds it, so you compute one: TF-IDF (term frequency × inverse document frequency)

Term in one maintenance logtfdf of 1,000 logslog(N/df)Weight
the121,0000.000.0
pump43001.204.8
cavitation2124.428.8
w = tf · log(N / df)N = 1,000 logs  ·  df = how many of them contain the term
The most frequent word scores zero. A person decided that is the right behavior

Learned FeaturesThe network learns the features and the classifier together

Fit your own encoder or reuse a versioned pretrained encoder

Case study: YouTube-8MThe dataset ships features, not videos

Feature extraction is also compression, and it is irreversible

Reduction

Three Branches of Reduction

Why Reduce at AllColumns, rows and bytes each cost something different

Removing rows or columns changes learning; lossless compression preserves the data

Fewer Columns

Extraction or SelectionKeep some original columns, or mix all of them into new ones

Selection keeps names you can read. Extraction keeps information you cannot name

Recap: PCA as a Fitted TransformReuse the training center and axes when new observations arrive

znew = (xnew − μtrain) Vtrain,k
Projection keeps selected directions and discards the rest

Demo: PCA Projection AngleTurn the axis and watch how much of the variation survives

1. Find a direction that keeps more variance.   2. Is retained variance enough to choose model features?

Answer: What PCA KeepsLarge retained variance does not guarantee useful predictive features

QuestionCheck
What survives?Variation along the chosen training axes
What disappears?Variation in discarded directions
Does the model still work?Evaluate with held-out observations
Validate the retained representation, not only its variance

Three Families of Feature SelectionCompare model use and relative fitting cost within one selection procedure

FamilyWhat it looks atModel fitsBlind spot
Filterthe columns alone, no modelnonea pair that only works together
Wrapperthe model’s score on a subsetmanythe search itself overfits
Embeddedthe model’s own coefficientsonethe answer is tied to that model
Compare cost, interactions and held-out performance before choosing a selection method

Wrapper Feature SelectionA wrapper compares feature subsets through repeated model fits

Train on training folds

temperature + current

Repeat within the same protocol
Repeated subset search can overfit the validation evidence

Embedded MethodsSome models select features during fitting; the result depends on the model and training data

FeatureIllustrative fitted coefficientInterpretation
Vibration0.8Used by this fitted model
Temperature0.3Used by this fitted model
Humidity0.0Removed by this fitted model
A zero coefficient describes one fitted model, not the absence of a real relationship

Fewer Rows

Sampling vs CurationBoth drop rows: sampling follows a design, curation follows quality

SamplingCuration
GoalA smaller set with known proportionsA better set: quality, consistency, coverage
TechniquesRandom, systematic, stratified, clusterFiltering for quality and coverage
Used forLess computation, class imbalanceTraining sets for large models, labeling budgets
ProportionsKept, or changed on purpose (imbalance)Changed by what the filters remove
Sampling decides which rows to keep; curation decides how good they must be

Sampling DesignThe selection rule determines which parts of the population survive

MethodHow rows are chosenFailure to check
Simple randomDraw rows at randomSmall groups may be missed
SystematicEvery kth recordA periodic list can align with k
StratifiedSample within each groupKeep the intended group proportions
ClusterSelect whole groupsOne factory may not represent the rest
Check the population structure before choosing the sampling rule

Sampling to Fix ImbalanceDropping majority rows raises the minority share from 17% to 44%

Resampling changes class prevalence. Evaluate and calibrate on the deployment distribution

Caveat: Survivorship BiasThe rows you kept are not the rows you lost

This shows the bombers that came back. Reinforce where there are no dots

Data CurationCuration filters for quality instead of sampling at random

This pipeline keeps 1.4% of the crawl as the training set

Fewer Bytes

Lossless or LossyCompression restores the original bit for bit, or only an approximation

The lossy box is smaller, and its changes stay

Lossless Master CopyKeep one lossless copy, because a lossy decision cannot be revisited

LosslessLossy
RestoresThe original, bit for bitAn approximation
Typical dataText, code, logs, tabularImages, audio, video
FormatsZIP, PNG, GZIP, Parquet with Snappy or ZstdJPEG, MP3; lossy H.264 / WebP
RatioLimited by entropyOften much higher, tunable
The catchSometimes not small enoughThe decision cannot be revisited
Text and logs stay lossless; media is where lossy pays

Fitting Preprocessing StepsFit on train, apply to test: every fitted step remembers something from the rows it saw

StepWhat it remembersWhat leaks if you fit on everything
Imputationthe column mediantest rows move the median
Scalingmean and standard deviationthe test spread enters every train row
Encodingthe list of categoriesa category that exists only in test
Binningthe bin edgesedges drawn around test values
Feature selectionthe columns keptcolumns kept because they help on test
PCAthe componentsaxes rotated to fit test variance
z = (x − μtrain) / σtrainthe same two numbers go to test and to every future row
Refit inside every fold; ship the final fit to testing and serving

Takeaway: Every transform and reduction is a decision
